source_title_hint: How To (actually) Fix Your Flat Feet
primary_summary: Flat feet are often misunderstood as a collapsed arch that must be "raised"; instead the foot uses pronation (arch lowering) as a normal motion. The foot can achieve this via two strategies – relative motion of the foot's bones/joints versus a whole‑foot orientation (dumping). A forward‑shifted centre of gravity forces more load onto the mid‑ and forefoot, flattening the arch over time. Restoring genuine pronation rather than relying on a single dumping strategy is the recommended corrective approach.

classification.usefulness_reason: Provides biomechanical concepts about flat feet and pronation useful for education and protocol design

problem_statements: Flat feet are often perceived as a collapse that must be corrected by raising the arch
A forward centre of gravity increases forefoot loading and can further flatten the foot
habits_or_contexts: relying solely on foot dumping during running
key_visual_points: Relative motion of foot joints vs whole‑foot orientation
Shift of centre of gravity backward to reduce forefoot load
advice_mentioned: Restore genuine pronation instead of compensatory pronation

knowledge_units.title: Flat‑foot misconception
knowledge_units.summary: Most people assume flat feet need a higher arch, but pronation (arch lowering) is a functional aspect of foot mechanics.
mechanisms: Foot pronation allows the arch to lower naturally during stance

knowledge_units.title: Two foot motion strategies
knowledge_units.summary: The foot can achieve pronation via (1) relative motion of its bones/joints or (2) whole‑foot orientation where the foot dumps onto the ground.
mechanisms: Relative motion maintains segmental movement; orientation collapses the foot as a single unit

knowledge_units.title: Effect of forward centre of gravity
knowledge_units.summary: Leaning forward shifts body weight onto the mid‑ and forefoot, which over time can flatten the arch and promote compensatory pronation.
mechanisms: Forward shift of COM increases load under forefoot
when_useful: Identifying gait patterns that exacerbate flat‑foot issues

knowledge_units.title: Restoring genuine pronation
knowledge_units.summary: Corrective work should focus on restoring true pronation rather than relying solely on foot dumping, by addressing why the foot is flat and shifting the centre of gravity backward.
mechanisms: Improving relative motion capacity of foot joints
